evidence: src/domain/order.ts: Order.advance and Order.cancel call nextStateOf and isCancellable from src/domain/order-state.ts, so the transition rules are defined only once.

src/domain/stock-reservation-service.ts: StockReservationService.reserve calls product.canReserve(quantity), the single definition in src/domain/product.ts, rather than repeating the stock comparison.

src/domain/stock-reservation-service.ts: the constructor injects ProductRepository (src/domain/product-repository.ts), and all reads and writes go through this.products.findById and this.products.save.
src/domain/order-item.ts requires quantity > 0; src/domain/product.ts requires initialStock >= 0. These are different invariants, not a duplicate.
src/domain/errors.ts, src/domain/id-generator.ts, src/domain/order-repository.ts and src/domain/product-repository.ts are the module's error types and ports, which fits the domain concern.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All files in src/domain serve one concern: the order and stock domain model. That covers the entities (Order, OrderItem, Product), the state machine (order-state.ts), the errors, the ports (OrderRepository, ProductRepository, IdGenerator) and a domain service (StockReservationService). Each rule is defined once. Order state transitions live in order-state.ts (NEXT_STATE, CANCELLABLE), and Order.advance and Order.cancel call nextStateOf and isCancellable rather than repeating the tables. The stock check lives in Product.canReserve. StockReservationService pre-checks by calling product.canReserve(quantity) so that it reserves all items or none. Its InsufficientStockError has the same message as the one in Product.reserve, but the rule is a call to one shared definition, not a copy. OrderItem requires a positive integer quantity; Product requires non-negative integer stock. These are different invariants, not a duplicate. StockReservationService reaches stored products only through the injected ProductRepository port. No file uses a database, ORM or query client, and none bypasses the module's abstractions.
